key_insight: The paper shows that explaining temporal graph neural networks requires tracing not only event embeddings but also the event-induced variables that carry long-range information flow.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more complete attribution tool for debugging, validating, and trusting temporal GNNs used in forecasting, tracing, and recommender-system pipelines.
method: Builds on the Normalized Relevance Measure (NRM) to quantify information flow from event embeddings and through event-induced variables.
Extends NRM with modular decomposition to construct relevance structures for complex ETGNN architectures.
Supports comparability of latent variables across layers and higher-order interaction analysis between events.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on two synthetic datasets for epidemic tracing and social dynamics plus a real-world political event network, where it outperformed existing explanation methods.
watch_item: The approach may be more complex to implement and interpret in large ETGNNs because it requires a full relevance-structure decomposition of the architecture.
paper_title: Explaining Temporal Graph Neural Networks via Feature-induced Information Flow
